name: The nebula of Wolf-Rayet star 134
subtitle: Single-image narrowband, SHO (Hubble) palette, RGB colour stars

facts.Optique: SharpStar 94EDPH refractor (94 mm aperture) with its dedicated reducer, 409 mm focal length (f/4.4)
facts.Caméra: QHY268M (monochrome), gain 56, offset 25, High Gain 2CMS mode, cooled to 0 °C, 1×1 binning

sections.title: Description
sections.html:
This 3.3° by 2.2° field, in the Cygnus Milky Way, is centred on WR 134, a Wolf-Rayet star: a massive, very hot star at the end of its life, losing its matter in a violent stellar wind. This wind has blown a bubble of gas around it, of which we mainly see a thin, bluish arc, shining in the ionized oxygen (OIII) line. It is the same phenomenon as in the Crescent Nebula (NGC 6888), about two degrees away, but much fainter.

Around the arc, the whole field is occupied by the great clouds of hydrogen and sulphur of the Cygnus region, crossed by filaments and areas of dark dust.

In the SHO palette, sulphur (SII) is assigned to red, hydrogen (Ha) to green and oxygen (OIII) to blue; the dominant green of the hydrogen is then toned down. The nebulae therefore do not have their real colours. The stars, on the other hand, come from short R, G and B exposures and have their true colours.

This image was acquired in collaboration with Renaud Venne-Landry.

sections.title: Acquisition
sections.html:
Location
Starfront remote site, Texas (31°32'51" N, 99°22'55" W)
Period
26 September to 22 November 2025
Camera
QHY268M (monochrome), gain 56, offset 25, High Gain 2CMS mode, cooled to 0 °C, 1×1 binning
Optics
SharpStar 94EDPH refractor (94 mm aperture) with its dedicated reducer, 409 mm focal length (f/4.4)
Image scale
1.90"/pixel (3.76 µm pixels)
Filters
Ha, OIII, SII for the nebulae; R, G, B for the stars
Software
Voyager (RoboTarget)

sections.title: Processing
sections.html:
Done in PixInsight 1.9.6.

Preprocessing

  • Calibration, alignment and stacking with WeightedBatchPreprocessing (Ha, OIII, SII, R, G, B masters).

Preparation

  • SHO combination (R = SII, G = Ha, B = OIII) for the nebulae.
  • RGB combination for the stars, with colour calibration on the stars in the field (SpectrophotometricColorCalibration, Gaia catalogue).
  • Common cropping of the edges.

Linear processing

  • BlurXTerminator (deconvolution), NoiseXTerminator (noise reduction).
  • StarXTerminator: the stars are removed from the SHO image and extracted from the RGB image.

Non-linear processing

  • Channel-by-channel stretch of the SHO image.
  • Green toned down (SCNR 0.7), contrast and saturation curves.
  • Addition of the RGB stars, stretched less than the nebulae.

Notes

  • The RGB frames are few (11 per filter): they are enough for the colour of the stars, not for a broadband image.
  • This image was produced before the DarkStructureEnhance finish and the lighter background setting were added.
